From the sounds of it, you have the same problem I did when I installed mint. My ethernet controller has spotty support with linux.

  1. Look up your motherboard on the internet and determine what NICs (network interface cards) are integrated with your motherboard. In my case, I have 2 Realtek RTL8111/8168/8411 gigabit NICs. You can probably find this out using device manager in windows. In linux, it's as easy as this:

    lspci | grep Ethernet 05:00.0 Ethernet controller: Realtek Semiconductor Co., Ltd. RTL8111/8168/8411 PCI Express Gigabit Ethernet Controller (rev 06)

  2. Go to the manufaturer's website and download the linux driver and install it post-install, or google your NIC model with the term "linux" and see what others have done.

This is the unfortunate part about linux sometimes. Installing drivers isn't typically the most user friendly.

Oh boy. Yep sounds like you have the same NICs as I do.

Here's one important thing I found... you absolutely cannot have any spaces in the path or realtek's scripts don't work.

What I mean is, you can't install this:

/home/you/my drivers for my nic/r182043/autorun.sh

This is because "my drivers for my nic" has spaces. If I recall correctly, is still doesn't work with the relative path (meaning, if you change directory into r182043 as per my above example.)

Instead, just plop the r182043 (or your number equivalent.. this is just a made up number!) in the root of your home folder (/home/your_username/) and try there. Mine just fired right up after executing autorun.sh.

One final note... you must run it as root. To do this, use sudo.

To summarize:

cd /home/username/r284955
sudo ./autorun.sh

Again, the paths are made up above, but just substitute as needed.
